title: Qt: Disable Multimedia
description:
Allow for QtMultimedia not to be present or being
actively disabled

notes.body:
I'm aware that integration of dialog to main window is not good idea, but I found no other way if VoIP windows should be singletons and it is essential new feature. BTW I studied other arrangements with use of QT signals and singletons looks more clear to me.
I'm open to try different design. All VoIP dialogs are now unified in term of opening them and calling other dialogs so it can be changed in row...

The issue here is the tight integration. We are overall working to make dialogs more "floaty" towards a MDI interface. With this integration it is no longer possible. I agree that singleton makes a lot of sense, but I would rather implement it using a factory in this case, where you have a calling mainwindow method which then collects from the factory, and the dialog handles the singleton internally.

On a side-note, why do you want to have a singleton in the first place? Does the functionality of the dialog depend on it? If so, you would break another principle, as in, dialogs stick around, even if the original trace has been closed. That makes comparisons between traces possible. If you have a singleton, the RTP/VoIP dialogs would behave differently then the rest of Wireshark dialogs.

Once again, I am sorry that I am bringing these issues up now. I was rather busy over the past year and missed it originally. I really LOVE the new dialogs and just want to bring them into the same direction as the rest of them (and yes, we have a looot of footwork to complete in that regard as well)

Factory method of dialog class is good idea. I will try to rewrite it to use it. In first I will handle compilation without QtMultimedia and then I will focus on it.

Why singleton VoIP dialogs?
The idea comes from me. I'm very often analysing voice traces where I have many (high houndrets/thousands) of calls and streams and I need to find relations between them and select just a few of it. They usually have no clear relation. Therefore I need to pick up a few from RTP Streams view, then a few from VoIP Calls (all for a call), then one or two from Sequence dialo, then remove some useless from list etc. And at the end I need to "compare" (understand play) selected streams together.
In past, it was possible to open RTP Player just once and it was modal. Therefore it was not possible to use other tools when it was opened. So I was looking for arrangement which was more flexible.
I found the idea of "playlist" - you can send streams from any tool to playlist to play it later.
Once there was playlist, someone (a dialog) need to maintain it and this dialog should be opened all the time by mi opinion. I decided to use RTP Player for it as it is the tool where streams from playlist should be "used".
In parallel to it I found that RTP Streams dialog as singleton is useful too. It shows all RTP streams, but you can select/deselect streams in it by other tools (VoIP Dialog, Sequence Dialog). Again, to remember selection, dialog must be opened all the time.
Once I implemented it, I'm very happy as I can pass streams between dialogs and filter interesting ones very fast and I'm able to do it at all - it was not possible before.

All VoIP dialogs are tested that if you close the capture, you see last content including possibility to play what is loaded in Player window. So I hope it works as before.
Player remembers playlist (rtpstream_id_t) when you open/start new capture. Therefore it allows you to show/select streams you already seen in past capture. It was not possible before.

Other point of view:
I think that VoIP dialogs were exceptional already. In past, it was possible to open e.g. RTP Streams window multiple times. But it made no sense because each window was cleared/reloaded on every retap. Therefore the idea that you have two windows with different content was not working there and it was just confusing IMHO. It was another reason why I changed it to singleton in this case.
BTW there was no filtering so you was really able just to open same window with same twice. I know that most of other dialogs are "better" and make sense to open them multiple times.

One more other point of view:
I'm not sure whether someone use VoIP dialogs as I do, but it looks to me more like toolbox with different views to same information - VoIP calls - than set of separate tools/windows. There were tools for cooperation already and I'm trying to push it forward too. 

I think you can work with dialogs as before - open and close it, if you don't need it. Singletonning of it is just advantage and another way how to use them.

When there will be more demand for opening same window multiple times to "freeze" current content, I propose to add button "Freeze" for VoIP dialogs which will do so. The reason is that all dialogs work with alive data now and refreshed with recaps etc. So making them frozen by default looks to me wrong idea, but I might be wrong too :-)

I understand your approach. Initially I was irritated with the current way playlists work, and I do think a lot of people are. It makes more sense if "Play" allowed for immediate play if no playlist has been defined yet (so in the background create one and add to it) and asks if the user wants to create a new playlist or add to the existing one if a playlist exists. Kind of how drag-drop with filter actions work currently, depending on an already applied display filter.

In its current state I think the dialog needs improvement from an UX perspective, but feature-wise it is sound. Keep in mind, that your workflow might not be a workflow someone else's envisions, and always try to imagine another persons ideas or way of work. Most people I know only listen to single streams to check if the issue is in the stream or on the playback device, so playsets will not be used. For those people the current iteration is an issue

Also I would very much appreciate if you can rework the way the dialog currently is implemented as a singleton, as it further complicates usage of main_window.

But for the underlying issue of this MR, I have no further inclination to hold it up

I see and I'm not so much happy I had to add one more level to allow a user to play stream, but I found no better way.
There is sequence how I developed it. I'm open to change it, if there is better UI arrangement:
My original idea was that if Play button pressed, do "Set" action on playlist - same as was before. But then I found there is no easy way how to create Add action and Remove action. Additional two separate buttons looks strange to me.
What about modify play button this way? When button pressed, it triggers Set playlist action. For Add/Remove there will be side menu. But I'm not sure right now whether I'm able to do it in Qt...

Rewriting to singleton is in my queue. I'm just waiting for merging this and then I have already one additional RTP Player related task done and will merge it after this one.

You may want to rebase this to current head as two of the recent patches to get Qt6 to compile touched the Multimedia_lib stuff (Qt6 currently only compiles with multimedia disabled).
You are more than welcome to make it work with Qt6 of course :-)
Apart from what I have written above, I like the aproach you took, it just needs adaption to the current codebase.
It looks like making QtMultimedia optional was added in !7206 as a part of Qt6Multimedia support.

commits_data.title: RTP Player: Can be compiled without QtMultimedia
commits_data.message:
RTP Player: Can be compiled without QtMultimedia

When no QtMultimedia available, player shows streams and waveform as
with QtMultimedia. All play functions are disabled, but export is
possible. Play rates are fixed, not detected from soundcard.

Placement of methods in code was slightly rearanged to group #ifdef together.

Documentation was updated.
